title: NOC SLA escalation & weekly sync
description: Weekly customer sync between Apex Athletics (Jax, Backend Engineer; Marcus, Account Manager; Deepa, Backend Engineer) and Owen from the National Olympic Training Center, covering last week's Kafka offset-commit SLA breach (ZD-101 / ENG-210, a recurrence of ENG-148) and the open data-sharing follow-up (ZD-102). Real org, tickets and incident facts are drawn from OrgForge; Owen (the customer-side speaker) is an authored stand-in since OrgForge does not name an individual NOC contact, only the org.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Thanks for jumping on, everyone — this is our weekly sync with National Olympic Training Center on the Apex Athletics telemetry rollout, and we also need to cover last week's SLA incident.

segments.speaker: Owen (National Olympic Training Center)
segments.text: Appreciate the time. Quick factual question before we start: wasn't there a similar Kafka offset issue back in early February, the one tracked as ENG-148? I want to know if this is a repeat.

segments.speaker: Jax
segments.text: Good memory. ENG-148 in early February was a misconfigured Kafka consumer group offset reset policy that forced the telemetry ingestion service to reprocess stale data and exhausted the Redis cache. What hit you last week, ZD-101 against ENG-210, is a different bug — a race condition in the offset-commit logic itself — but it's flagged as a recurrence pattern of ENG-148.

segments.speaker: Deepa
segments.text: To be precise, ENG-210 stalled the offset commits and built a backlog that breached our sub-100ms latency SLA for about forty minutes before we caught it.

segments.speaker: Owen (National Olympic Training Center)
segments.text: Forty minutes matters during a training block. What's the actual fix, not just the patch?

segments.speaker: Jax
segments.text: We're weighing two approaches. Approach A moves the consumer group to idempotent, exactly-once offset commits instead of the at-least-once mode we run today — more thorough, but it touches the whole consumer library. Approach B keeps at-least-once and adds a dead-letter queue plus tighter consumer-lag alerting so we catch a stall before it breaches SLA.

segments.speaker: Deepa
segments.text: We already validated the DLQ pattern for approach B during the kafka scaling architecture review, so it's the faster path to ship safely.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Given the championship season starting next month, let's decide now instead of dragging this out.

segments.speaker: Jax
segments.text: Decision: we'll go with approach B. It ships faster and the DLQ gives us a stronger safety net than the reprocessing risk of moving every consumer to exactly-once under load.

segments.speaker: Owen (National Olympic Training Center)
segments.text: Understood. I do want to flag this is the second SLA breach this quarter, and under our SLA-backed telemetry reliability agreement that's grounds for a service credit.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: You're right, and I don't want to make you fight for it. I'm going to offer National Olympic Training Center a 20% discount on next quarter's telemetry reliability fee for the ENG-210 breach.

segments.speaker: Owen (National Olympic Training Center)
segments.text: Thank you, that's fair. I'd like it in writing so our finance team has a record.

segments.speaker: Jax
segments.text: I'll send a follow-up email today summarizing the root cause and the fix we're taking so you have it in writing.

segments.speaker: Deepa
segments.text: I'll open a ticket for Ben to add consumer-lag alerting on the offset-commit path before we touch anything else, so we get an early warning next time.

segments.speaker: Owen (National Olympic Training Center)
segments.text: Good — can we get a checkpoint before the championship goes live? Let's sync again next Tuesday.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Works for us, I'll send the invite.

segments.speaker: Jax
segments.text: One more thing on our side — between this incident response and the kafka scaling work, our on-call rotation is stretched thin. We're short-handed on backend right now and need to hire another backend engineer to cover the Kafka on-call load.

segments.speaker: Deepa
segments.text: Agreed, we've paged the same three people for every incident this quarter.

segments.speaker: Owen (National Olympic Training Center)
segments.text: That's on your side, not blocking us. One more idea while we're all here — we could maybe consider rewriting the whole ingestion service someday, if the JVM overhead ever becomes the real bottleneck.

segments.speaker: Jax
segments.text: Noted, but that's not on the roadmap right now — we'd only revisit it if profiling showed the runtime itself was the ceiling.

segments.speaker: Owen (National Olympic Training Center)
segments.text: Separate question — did the data-sharing follow-up tracked as ZD-102 ever get closed out, or is that still open on your side?

segments.speaker: Jax
segments.text: Let me check... yes, ZD-102 is still open, we owe National Olympic Training Center a written answer on the export cadence, daily versus weekly snapshots.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: I'll fold that into the same follow-up note so you get one email instead of two.

segments.speaker: Deepa
segments.text: On the alerting ticket, I'll scope it to just the offset-commit path for now, we can widen it later if we see the same pattern elsewhere.

segments.speaker: Owen (National Olympic Training Center)
segments.text: That's a sensible scope.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Anything else before we wrap?

segments.speaker: Owen (National Olympic Training Center)
segments.text: No, this was thorough — thanks for owning it.

segments.speaker: Jax
segments.text: Thanks everyone. To recap: root cause is the ENG-210 recurrence of ENG-148, we're shipping approach B, Marcus is issuing the 20% discount, I'm sending the written follow-up, Deepa's opening the alerting ticket for Ben, and we reconvene next Tuesday.

segments.speaker: Marcus
segments.text: Sounds good, talk soon.
